requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH: drawer at 1,1 (half-s base, drawer:0#1,1#cut) fills the junction 0,1|1,0|1,1. Attempt to add spike at same junction (socket s85) refused: 'a drawer (north half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand. Take the drawer off, or use another junction.' Only alternative s86 is different corner 0,0|0,1|1,0, not same cell/corner. Current build has drawer only; meshClash clear but coexistence impossible by rule.

finish.summary: Requirement unmet due to configurator rule. Verified drawer placement then spike at same corner rejected with SPIKE_CLASH.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
The configurator forbids a spike and a drawer occupying the same junction — the drawer physically fills the corner where the spike would stand.

Build attempt to verify:
- Placed bases at 0,0 + 1,0 + 0,1 to create junctions.
- Placed drawer on half base at 1,1 (key `n` via socket s83) → `drawer:0#1,1#cut`.
- Attempted `addSpike` at the same/same-cell-touching junction `0,1|1,0|1,1` (socket s85) → refused `SPIKE_CLASH`: *“a drawer (north half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand. Take the drawer off, or use another junction.”*
- Only alternative offered (s86 at `0,0|0,1|1,0`) is a different corner/cell — not the brief.

check_build: `ok:true`, `meshClash:clear`, LOOSE_BODY warnings only.

I did not place a spike at a different junction, as that would falsely claim the requirement was met.
